description: Anthropic model prices and cache cost multipliers used by the session-efficiency auditor. Data only: no code lives here, and nothing in this file is derived at runtime.

consumers.src/pricing.js: models -> per-session USD conversion of estWasteTokens
consumers.src/rules.js: cacheMultipliers -> the PRICE constant behind the waste model

cacheMultipliers.description: Relative cost per input token. A cached prefix read costs 0.1x; a prefix that must be rewritten costs 1.25x. The gap between them is what every cache-waste rule prices.

pseudoModels.description: Model-id slots in the session log that are not models. Claude Code stamps these on assistant entries it generated locally (interrupt notices, API-error replies): no API call, zero tokens in every usage field. Excluded from rate blending entirely — counting them as unpriced would put a spurious disclosure on every report, and counting them as $0 would drag a session's blended rate down.

reference.description: Documented for humans, deliberately not read by any code. Adding a consumer for anything here means moving it into a section above.

fastMode.note: Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 with speed=fast are billed at a premium. Session logs record the model id but not the speed parameter, so a fast-mode turn is indistinguishable from a standard one and is priced at the standard rate. Dollar figures are therefore a floor on any workload that used fast mode.

unpricedModels.note: Legacy ids that may appear in older session logs and have no published rate in the current reference. They are NOT given a fallback rate: a session on one of these contributes tokens to the headline and nothing to the dollar figure, and the omission surfaces as manifest.pricing.pricedWasteShare. A visible gap is a smaller error than a plausible wrong dollar. To price one, move it into `models` with a sourced rate.

idNormalization.note: Session logs carry deployment ids, not the bare model id. Two suffixes are stripped before lookup, so only base ids belong in `models`.
